title: Memphis logotype drawing
lede: Christoph Radl’s artwork for the Memphis wordmark: squared white capitals over a patterned underline.
summary: Radl’s 1982 drawing of the blocky MEMPHIS wordmark on black.

creator.name: Christoph Radl (designer); Sottsass Associati and Memphis (clients)

evidence.note: Downloaded the museum’s published image (640 × 466 px) from [the Stedelijk Museum](https://www.stedelijk.nl/en/collection/92798-christoph-radl-memphis) to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The museum’s file carries a “NO REPRO QUALITY” stamp.

styles.note: The group’s own wordmark, drawn by its graphic designer.

context: The Stedelijk classes this as a drawing by Christoph Radl, 1982, 34.7 × 47.5 cm, with Sottsass Associati and Memphis as clients. [Stedelijk record](https://www.stedelijk.nl/en/collection/92798-christoph-radl-memphis).

*Interni* says Radl began working with Ettore Sottsass in 1980, “designing the image of Memphis”, and later curated the 2022 Triennale exhibition “Memphis Again”. [Interni: Memphis Again](https://www.internimagazine.com/agenda/memphis-again/).
observed: White capitals “MEMPHIS” sit on a black rectangle mounted on a white board.
The letters are built from rectangles; the M has a notched, stepped middle, and some strokes end in angled cuts.
Under each letter group runs a short bar of fine black-and-white pattern, broken into segments.
Tape and registration marks around the board show that it is working artwork.
interpretation: The wordmark is heavy and simple, which lets it sit on top of the group’s busy patterns. The patterned underline brings the laminate language into the type.
borrow: Pair a heavy, squared display wordmark with a thin patterned rule under it.
Put the wordmark in white on a solid black band when it must work over pattern.
related: The same letterforms appear on the [Memphis swatch card](ref:memphis-printed-cotton-swatch-1985) and the [1983 leaflet](ref:radl-memphis-milano-leaflet-1983).

rights.statement: The Stedelijk links to a general copyright page; no open license is stated. No image is stored.
